{"rules": ["Model consistently underestimates price spikes during high volatility periods (e.g., Nov 2022), failing to capture sudden upward momentum despite low sentiment scores.", "Forecast shows significant lag in reacting to recent price increases; true outcomes often exceed the last known price by 5-10% within the first week of the forecast horizon.", "Model exhibits mean-reversion bias, predicting a smooth linear trend that ignores the erratic, high-frequency fluctuations seen in actual market data.", "When sentiment is near zero but recent history shows strong upward drift (e.g., Examples 2-4), the model fails to extrapolate this momentum, resulting in systematic undershoot.", "Forecast horizon errors are non-linear: early days of the forecast period show large negative bias relative to true outcomes, which may stabilize or reverse later.", "Low sentiment scores do not correlate with price stability; sudden spikes occur even when sentiment history remains flat, indicating a need for volatility-aware correction."]
